AFWD.chosen_element: tortoise step x ← f(x) mod N and hare step y ← f(f(y)) mod N
AFWD.justification: forward morphism advancing both walkers along the functional graph defined by f(x) = x² + c mod N

AREV.chosen_element: backward walk through the polynomial iteration x ← x² + c mod N
AREV.justification: contravariant descent that re-traverses the functional graph in reverse to expose the cycle structure

CLINK.chosen_element: sequential chaining of tortoise and hare steps into a single iteration round
CLINK.justification: composition that binds one tortoise advance and two hare advances into one atomic cycle-detection tick

ENGAGR.chosen_element: x ≡ y (mod p) ∧ x ≢ y (mod N) held simultaneously
ENGAGR.justification: dialetheia: the walkers are equal modulo a hidden factor and unequal modulo the composite — both true at once, the engine's paradox

EVALF.chosen_element: tortoise ≢ hare (mod N) while GCD(|x - y|, N) = 1
EVALF.justification: negative arm: the walkers differ modulo the full composite, yielding no factor yet

EVALT.chosen_element: tortoise ≡ hare (mod p) for some prime factor p of N
EVALT.justification: affirmative arm: the walkers have collided inside the cycle modulo a true factor

FFUSE.chosen_element: GCD(|x - y|, N) computed when tortoise and hare positions coincide modulo a factor
FFUSE.justification: the arms rejoin by collapsing the dialetheia into a concrete divisor; conflicting congruences fuse to a factor or 1

FSPLIT.chosen_element: initialization of tortoise and hare walkers at the same seed x₀
FSPLIT.justification: one state opens into two arms: the slow pointer (tortoise) and the fast pointer (hare) that will diverge in step count

IFIX.chosen_element: append-only log of (iteration, tortoise, hare, GCD) tuples
IFIX.justification: permanent, irreversible record of every cycle-detection tick; cannot be undone or rewritten

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: the polynomial f(x) = x² + c mod N as a self-recognizing object
IMSCRIB.justification: identity: the iteration function is itself the structure it generates; inserting it leaves the verdict untouched

TANCH.chosen_element: non-trivial factor d of N or the sealed report of failure
TANCH.justification: the closed boundary that contains the entire extraction; once d is fixed or the cycle exhausts, the engine halts

VINIT.chosen_element: uninitialized state before N is named
VINIT.justification: no walkers, no polynomial, no modulus — the void prior to any arithmetic object

phase_2.fuse_element: GCD(|x - y|, N) computed when tortoise and hare positions coincide modulo a factor
phase_2.fuse_result: non-trivial factor d of N, or 1 triggering restart with new c, or N indicating failure
phase_2.rejoin_note: tortoise and hare arms advance at different rates through the functional graph; when they meet modulo a factor p, the dialetheia x≡y(mod p)∧x≢y(mod N) is held by ENGAGR; FFUSE extracts GCD(|x-y|,N) collapsing the paradox into a factor; if GCD=1 the fork reopens with new polynomial parameter c; if GCD=N the fork stays open permanently (open fork, verdict B or N)
phase_2.split_element: initialization of tortoise and hare walkers at the same seed x₀
phase_2.split_input: composite integer N, polynomial f(x) = x² + c mod N, initial seed x₀
split_outputs: tortoise arm: x ← f(x) mod N (one step per round)
hare arm: y ← f(f(y)) mod N (two steps per round)
phase_2.verdict_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.both_description: B4 B (11) — both held at once: a live contradiction, the paraconsistent resolution
phase_3.void_description: B4 N (00) — neither: uninitialized, nothing established
